# Use the code segment below #11 - #13

```
int main(void)
{
   char x = '9';
   int y = 2;
   int z;

   z = x++ * y - 7 * y;
   printf("x: %c\n", x);
   printf("z: %d\n", z);

   return (0);
}
```

# 11. What is the FIRST line of output generated by the program above?

+   A) x: .
+   B) x: 0
+   C) x: 10
+   D) None of the above.

# 12. What is the SECOND line of output generated by the program above?

+   A) z: 6
+   B) z: 100
+   C) z: -570
+   D) None of the above.

# 13. Which of the following could replace line #7 and would not alter the output produced by lines #9 - #10?

+   A) z = (x * y) - (7 * y);
+   B) z = x++ * (y - 7) * y;
+   C) z = (x++ * y) - (7 * y);
+   D) None of the above.

+   B) A character constant is a literal constant consisting of a character enclosed in single quotes.
+   C) Defined constants are preprocessor directives.
+   D) None of the above.
